The midnight sun appears at- (a) North Pole (b) South Pole (c) Equator (d) Tropic of Cancer U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1990 Ans. (a & b) The midnight sun is a natural phenomenon that occurs in places north of the Arctic Circle or south of the Antarctic Circle. Between these circles and the poles, the sun is visible for the full 24 hours. Accordingly, in countries like Norway, situated north to the Arctic Circle, the sun is visible even during the night. This is why Norway is known as the country of the midnight sun. Parts of other countries like Canada, Finland, Russia and Iceland also fall north to the Arctic Circle. Mindanao is an island in the Philippines archipelago. The Hydrosphere *The Hydrosphere is the total mass of water on the surface of our planet. Although the Earth’s Hydrosphere has been around for longer than 4 billion years, it continues to change rise. This is caused by seaﬂ oor spreading and continental drift. Hydrosphere occupies 2/3rd of the total surface of the Earth. *Ocean water covers about 70.0% of Earth’s surface. There is only one world ocean but the continents divide the ocean into ﬁ ve distinct parts - (i) Paciﬁ c Ocean (165.2 million sq. km.) (ii) Atlantic Ocean (106.4 million sq. km.) (iii) Indian ocean (73.6 million sq. km.) (iv) Antarctic Ocean (2.6 - 18.8 million sq. km.) The Paciﬁ c Ocean is the largest ocean in the world. High Mountain Average Height Sea Floar Area *The Oceanic Relief has more diversity as compared to Lithosphere Relief. *The Hypsographic Curve is a scientiﬁ c way of describing the topography of the seaﬂ oor we read the hypsographic curve like a graph with an x-axis (horizontal) and a y-axis (vertical). The x-axis tells us the elevation of the province. The curved line on the graph tells us about the provinces - where we see a change in the slope of the line, we are looking at a diﬀ erent province. *The oceanic crust diﬀ ers strikingly from the continental crust with respect to rock types, structure, landforms, age and origin. Four major divisions in the ocean relief are- 1. Continental Shelf - It is the submerged margin of continental mass extending from the shore to the ﬁ rst prominent slope. 2. Continental Slope - The slope that extends from the continental shelf down to the ocean deep. 3. Continental Rise - This is the gently sloping seaﬂ oor lying at the foot of the continental slope leading gradually into the Abyssal Plain. 4. Abyssal Floor - This is the large expanse of very smooth ocean ﬂ oor found at depths of 3000 to 6000 mts. In fact they are the most widespread landforms on the earth and occupy almost 76% of the total oceanic area. *Oceanic Trenches are narrow, deep depression in the seafloor representing the line of the subduction of an oceanic lithosphere plate. The ocean trenches are the lowest areas on Earth’s Surface and occupy almost 7% of Ocean’s Relief. They have very steep slopes. Examples of Oceanic Trenches are Marina Trench (Challenger Deep), Tonga, Kuril-Kamchatka, etc. other important oceanic reliefs are - (i) Oceanic Ridge - forms by lava which erupts beneath the sea and cools to form solid rocks. (ii) Mid Oceanic Ridge - is an under water mountain system formed by plate tectonics. (iii) Guyot - a Guyot, also known as a tablemount is an isolated underwater volcanic mountain with a ﬂ oating top below the surface of the sea. They are commonly found in the Paciﬁ c Ocean, but they have been identiﬁ ed in all the oceans except the Arctic Ocean. (iv) Submarine Canyon - Narrow steep sided valleys that cut into continental slopes and continental rises of the ocean. (v) Fracture Zone - is a linear Oceanic feature often hundreds, even thousands of kilometres long. They are a consequence of Plate Tectonics. Similarly, other Ocean Relief Features include Island Arcs, Atolls, Coral Reefs, submerged volcanoes, sea-scarps etc. *The Mid Atlantic Ridge is a mid-ocean ridge, a divergent Join−> https://t.me/thehindu000 CB–108 General Studies World Geography tectonic plate or constructive plate boundary located on the ﬂ oor of the Atlantic Ocean and part of the longest mountain range in the world. In the North Atlantic it seperates the Eurasian and North American plates and in South Atlantic it seperates the African & South American plates. *The ninety east ridge is a ridge on the Indian Ocean ﬂ oor named for its near parallel strike along the 90th meridian at the centre of the Eastern Hemisphere. *Example of such islands in the Indian Ocean are - Laccadive, Maldives, Chagos, New Amsterdam, Saint Paul, Karguelen, etc. *Datum line is that horizontal line used to measure heights and depths. *97% of the total water present on the planet is saline in nature. The remaining 3% is fresh water. Out of this 3%, 2.4% are in the form of Glaciers and polar ice. Hence, less than 1% of fresh water resource is available for use. *Out of the total available fresh water, 68.7% is inaccessible as they are in form of glaciers and ice caps. 30.1% is in the form of groundwater, 0.3% is in the form of Surface water and only 0.9% are in the form of other available sources. 1. Important Seas of the World In terms of Geography, a sea is a part of the ocean partially enclosed by land. Seas are smaller than the oceans and are usually located where the land and ocean meet. Some important seas of the world are as follows- *The South China Sea is a marginal sea which is a part of the Paciﬁ c Ocean. It is located between China, Taiwan, Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei, Indonesia and Vietnam. Its maximum depth is 5,016 mts. *The Bering Sea is also a marginal sea of the Paciﬁ c Ocean. Covering a total area of 884900 sq. km, it has a maximum depth of 4773 mts. *Mediterranean sea is a sea connected to the Atlantic Ocean. It is largest of all seas enclosed by land. It extends between North Africa, Southern Europe, Anatolia and Levant. The maximum known depth of the Mediterranean sea is 4632 mts. *The Black Sea is a marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean. Located in the south-east the Black Sea is surrounded by Europe, Caucasus and Anatolia Peninsula (Turkey). *The Caspian sea is the world’s largest inland body of water, and world’s largest salt water lake. It is also the world’s largest lake. It covers a total area of 371000 sq. km. It has borders with Russia, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Kazakhstan. *The sea of Azov is a sea in Eastern Europe, which is almost completely enclosed by land, having just a narrow opening into the Black Sea via Strait of Kerch. The sea borders Ukraine in North, Russia in the east and Crimea in the west. *The Aral sea is an important water body of the middle east. It lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. *Sargasso sea is a water body in the North Atlantic ocean. The sea is bounded by Gulf stream on the west, North Atlantic Current on the North, Canary Current in the East and North Atlantic Equatorial Current on the south. The sea is named after the brown Sargasso seaweed, which is found in abundance in the region.
